answer: Agents can earn influence only through repeated, escrowed exchanges with randomly assigned peers, and each peer can endorse an exchange only after independently verifying delivery. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one account into a spiral of aliases does not multiply trust; colluding aliases mostly create an echo, since they cannot supply independent counterparties. To gain influence, an attacker must fund many real trades and risk losing escrow on disputes, making a Sybil campaign costly and slow rather than a quick wander through fresh accounts.
